lesson_scope: Multi-stage rectilinear and inclined-plane motion with piecewise constant accelerations; dynamics and kinematics of bodies moving on smooth and rough slopes under gravity; transition between atmospheric free-fall and fluid immersion with resistive deceleration; velocity-time graph sketching and kinematic coordinate determination for connected stages.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 1: Sliding down a smooth incline from rest

$$a = g\sin 30^\circ = 10(0.5) = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

$$a = 10\sin 30^\circ = 5\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

Compute final velocity:
- Applying suvat down the $10\text{ m}$ track:
$$v^2 = 2(5)(10) = 100 \implies v = 10\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The particle accelerates at $5\text{ m s}^{-2}$ to reach $10\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Drill 3: Net deceleration of a body entering a viscous liquid

hints: In the liquid, two forces act: downward gravity $W = mg = 0.2(10) = 2\text{ N}$ and upward resistance $3.6\text{ N}$.
Net upward force is $3.6 - 2.0 = 1.6\text{ N}$. Apply Newton's second law $F = ma$ to find deceleration: $a = \frac{1.6}{0.2} = 8\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

walkthrough.text:
Calculate the downward gravitational force and the resultant vertical force:
$$W = mg = 0.2(10) = 2\text{ N}$$
$$F_{\text{net}} = R - W = 3.6 - 2 = 1.6\text{ N} \text{ upwards}$$

Apply Newton's second law to find the magnitude of deceleration:
$$a = \frac{F_{\text{net}}}{m} = \frac{1.6}{0.2} = 8\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
$$\text{Deceleration is } 8\text{ m s}^{-2}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Identify vertical forces inside the liquid:
- Gravity pulls down with $2\text{ N}$ while liquid resists with $3.6\text{ N}$:
$$F_{\text{net}} = 3.6 - 2.0 = 1.6\text{ N} \text{ upwards}$$

Compute braking acceleration:
- Dividing resultant force by mass:
$$a = \frac{1.6}{0.2} = 8\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
The liquid produces an upward braking deceleration of $8\text{ m s}^{-2}$.

questions.difficulty_reason: Structured Practice: Core Practice 3: Constant deceleration along successive equal intervals of an incline

source_evidence.structural_inspiration: Core Practice 3: Constant deceleration along successive equal intervals of an incline

hints: Apply $s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$ to the first section $PQ$ with $s = 2.4\text{ m}$ and $t = 0.6\text{ s}$.
For section $PQ$: $2.4 = 0.6u + 0.18a$, which simplifies to $40 = 10u + 3a$.
Consider the combined journey from $P$ to $R$: distance is $2.4 + 2.4 = 4.8\text{ m}$ and time is $0.6 + 1.0 = 1.6\text{ s}$.
For section $PR$: $4.8 = 1.6u + 1.28a$, which simplifies to $3 = u + 0.8a$. Solve the two linear equations to find $a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and $u = 4.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

walkthrough.text:
Set up the displacement equation for the section $PQ$ with $s = 2.4\text{ m}$ and $t = 0.6\text{ s}$:
$$s = ut + \frac{1}{2}at^2$$
$$2.4 = 0.6u + \frac{1}{2}a(0.6^2) = 0.6u + 0.18a$$
$$40 = 10u + 3a \quad \text{--- (Equation 1)}$$

Set up the displacement equation for the combined interval $PR$ with $s = 4.8\text{ m}$ and $t = 0.6 + 1.0 = 1.6\text{ s}$:
$$4.8 = 1.6u + \frac{1}{2}a(1.6^2) = 1.6u + 1.28a$$
$$3 = u + 0.8a \implies u = 3 - 0.8a \quad \text{--- (Equation 2)}$$
Substitute Equation 2 into Equation 1:
$$40 = 10(3 - 0.8a) + 3a = 30 - 8a + 3a = 30 - 5a$$
$$5a = -10 \implies a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
$$\text{Deceleration is } 2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
Substitute $a = -2$ into Equation 2:
$$u = 3 - 0.8(-2) = 3 + 1.6 = 4.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$

teacher_walkthrough.text:
Express distances in terms of $u$ and acceleration $a$:
- Over $PQ$ ($0.6\text{ s}$):
$$2.4 = 0.6u + 0.18a \implies 10u + 3a = 40$$
- Over $PR$ ($1.6\text{ s}$):
$$4.8 = 1.6u + 1.28a \implies u + 0.8a = 3$$

Solve the linear system:
- Substituting $u = 3 - 0.8a$ into the first relation:
$$10(3 - 0.8a) + 3a = 40 \implies 30 - 5a = 40 \implies a = -2\text{ m s}^{-2}$$
- Back-substituting yields:
$$u = 3 - 0.8(-2) = 4.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$$
The particle decelerates at $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ with initial velocity $4.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.

ai_rubric.observable: Sets up displacement equation for interval $PQ$: $2.4 = 0.6u + 0.18a$.
Sets up displacement equation for full interval $PR$: $4.8 = 1.6u + 1.28a$.
Solves simultaneous equations to obtain deceleration $2\text{ m s}^{-2}$ and initial speed $u = 4.6\text{ m s}^{-1}$.
